doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

title: Chico Hamilton, Mulligan and the pianoless quartet
summary: Poston discusses the tension between Hamilton and Mulligan and how the pianoless quartet came about.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well Chico said that the Gerry Mulligan Quartet was almost the same thing. It was no stroke of genius, it started in my living room and critics/historians everyone wants to make it something like a genius thing, and that’s B.S. he said.

Yeah I mean there’s some of that. Chico and Gerry didn’t get along too well after Chico left. And you would think that years later they would have let that go. Well Gerry didn’t let things go very well. But Chico left the group to go with Lena Horne when the group had really hit you know. And Gerry just really kind of — you know Gerry would say that’s all in the past, but then when you really talked to him off the record he never — because to him they had created this very special thing and Chico was a major part of that. And then when Chico left that group to go with Lena Horne, Gerry never really let it go too much. And that’s what’s funny too because I had many events where I would have the two of them with their own groups on the same event and they crossed paths but they really weren’t too friendly so it was really true. But then you know I talked to Chico after Gerry died and Chico was very — I think it was more on Gerry’s side probably than Chico’s because Chico spoke at Gerry’s memorial and you know he spoke very highly of him. But there was a little — there was that tension there. But Chico is correct in that it came together out of the necessity of the piano not being available when Gerry was offered. So I have no doubt. But the reality is Gerry had been thinking in those terms and this just made it make sense. A piano wasn’t going to be available therefore if you could work without the piano you can have the job, and Gerry had been thinking along those terms so then they started to — and then it just turned out to be this once-in-a-lifetime miraculous thing that came together that wouldn’t have come together probably with any other pieces of that puzzle you know. that, it just — I think it just made it work because you know Chet’s role was a necessity, Bob Whitlock’s role was a necessity, much more so than he gets credit for, and of course Chico’s as well.
